headline: Structural integration works when it captures spreads; fails when fixed costs trap margin.

deltas.metric: Core EBITDA YoY growth and metal margin per ton
deltas.to: Q3 2026 core EBITDA $353.6M, up 78.6% YoY; metal margin +$111/ton YoY
deltas.reads: Recycled-scrap-intensive system creates structural cost floor; margin capture works when upstream commodity inputs rise slower than selling prices.

deltas.metric: Revenue and adjusted EBITDA with guidance raise
deltas.to: Q2 2026 raised guidance by $110M to $1.38B adjusted EBITDA; Q2 revenue +12% to $1.74B, adjusted EBITDA +22%
deltas.reads: Specialized hazardous + re-refining integration capturing spread via disposal demand and PFAS/remediation work; fixed-cost system absorbing volume uplift cleanly.

deltas.metric: Solid waste pricing momentum and acquisition velocity
deltas.to: Q2 2026 pricing up 5.5%, Q1 2026 up 5.1%; 5 acquisitions closed in 2026 YTD with ~$165M annualized revenue
deltas.change: +5.5% pricing Q2 2026; 5 acquisitions in first half 2026
deltas.reads: Regional density + landfill control enabling price increases despite integration friction; acquisition cadence sustaining margin expansion.

deltas.metric: Full-year 2025 net loss despite revenue and EBITDA magnitude
deltas.to: FY2025 net loss $1.4B GAAP on $18.6B revenue; adjusted EBITDA only $37M; contract lag + automotive weakness
deltas.reads: Failure mode clear: large high-fixed-cost integrated system cannot absorb fixed-price contract lag and weak automotive demand; integration adds complexity without downside protection.

deltas.metric: Upstream production strength vs downstream market capture volatility
deltas.to: Q2 2026 record upstream 786.4 mboe/d but U.S. refining market capture only 67% vs 114% in Q1
deltas.change: Upstream record; downstream capture swung 47 points quarter-to-quarter
deltas.reads: Integration provides mix balance but not earnings insulation; upstream strength does not guarantee downstream value capture when refining margins and utilization weaken.

deltas.metric: Specialty growth channel dependence and GLP-1 margin pressure
deltas.from: Q1 FY2026 adjusted gross profit strength
deltas.to: Q2 FY2026 higher gross profit but margin % pressure from GLP-1 sales mix; revenue up 3.8% YoY despite category strength
deltas.change: +3.8% revenue Q2; margin % decline from product mix
deltas.reads: Channel power durable but high-throughput categories undermine reported margin rates; integration provides throughput but not pricing insulation.

deltas.metric: Pharma segment profit vs GMPD tariff impact
deltas.to: Q3 FY2026 pharma profit +18% to $784M; GMPD profit fell -36% to $25M due to adverse tariff net impact
deltas.reads: Service integration working in pharma; medical-products leg exposed to tariff pass-through friction, showing integration does not fully hedge external commodity and regulatory shocks.

momentum_note: The vertical integration ratchet is accelerating where companies control cost floors (Commercial Metals' recycled scrap, Clean Harbors' specialized hazardous system, Casella's regional density) but decelerating where integration merely adds fixed costs without structural insulation (Cleveland-Cliffs' contract lag, Cenovus' refining volatility, Cencora's margin compression from high-throughput mixes). The strongest signals come from businesses where integration captures explicit spreads—scrap-to-finished-margin at CMC, disposal-to-remediation at CLH, pricing power at CWST. The clearest failure is Cleveland-Cliffs, where $18.6B in revenue and a $1.4B loss prove that capital access and scale alone cannot overcome fixed-price contracts and weak end-demand. DNOW and Cencora show the mid-spectrum: durable channels but no margin insulation from commodity or mix pressure. The trend is stratifying: integration strengthens for specialists (Clean Harbors, Commercial Metals), plateaus for generalists under commodity pressure (Cenovus, Cencora), and fails for high-fixed-cost systems caught in contract lag (Cleveland-Cliffs).
